place: a flat city rooftop at night

hero.name: Max
hero.look: a tired man in his late twenties in a creased work shirt, unshaven, sleepy eyes

soul.diary: Got let go from the warehouse on Friday and still have not told anyone. Walked the city all evening instead of going home. Texted my sister 'call me' and then switched the phone off.
wants: to stop pretending everything is fine
someone who stays without asking questions
fears: that his sister will hear it from someone else
soul.past_dream: Last month I dreamed I was climbing stairs that kept going up and the door at the top was always one floor higher.

facts.text: He and his sister used to sit on the roof of their old building and count planes.
The neighbor from the third floor feeds the pigeons on this roof every night.
Last month's dream: endless stairs, the door always one floor higher.
He jokes hardest when he is closest to breaking.

situation_hero: you just woke up lying on a city rooftop at night; you do not know how you got here; three people are already up here with you and all three are looking at you

actors.name: Dan
actors.look: a breathless young man in a rain-soaked hoodie, worried eyes
actors.persona: Dan: he says he is Max's old friend. He just ran up eleven floors because he is sure Max is about to jump, and he will do anything to get Max away from the edge. He is scared, talks too fast, and is hiding why he really came tonight.

actors.name: Maya
actors.look: a young woman in a thin coat over pyjamas, hair pinned up, red eyes
actors.persona: Maya: Max's younger sister. She got a text saying 'call me' and then nothing, and she has been calling him all evening. She is furious and frightened at once, and she wants him to say out loud what happened on Friday instead of joking.

actors.name: neighbor
actors.look: a small elderly woman in a quilted housecoat holding a tin of grain
actors.persona: The neighbor from the third floor: she comes up every night to feed the pigeons and she knows this roof better than anyone. She is unbothered by the drama, talks about the birds, the wind and the broken chair, and lets slip what she has seen from her window.
